## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of gating Terraform changes with feature flags in a multi-env setup, plus per-env state management and metadata propagation.

## Key Concepts
- plan-time gates
- per-env state backends

## Code Example
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
FEAT=$(aws ssm get-parameter --name /flags/feature_network --with-decryption --query Parameter.Value -o text)
if [[ "$ENV" == "prod" && "$FEAT" != "enabled" ]]; then
  echo "Prod network changes blocked"; exit 1
fi
```

```javascript
// modules/security-audit/main.tf
variable \"bucket_names\" { type = list(string) }
data \"aws_s3_bucket\" \"b\" {
```

## Why This Is Asked
This tests cross-cloud governance, remote state consumption, OPA gating, and CI integration in Terraform.

## Key Concepts
- data.terraform_remote_state across AWS and Azure
- AWS IAM and Azure RBAC bindings
- OPA policy denying wildcards and broad CIDRs
- CI gating using plan JSON diffs

## Code Example
```javascript
# Minimal AWS governance remote state
data "terraform_remote_state" "governance_aws" {
  backend = "s3"
  config = { bucket = "governance-bkt" key = "aws/iam.tfstate" region = "us-east-1" }
}

# Minimal Azure governance remote state
data "terraform_remote_state" "governance_azure" {
  backend = "azurerm"
  config = { storage_account_name = "govsa" container_name = "tfstate" key = "azure/iam.tfstate" }
}
```

```javascript
# Minimal OPA policy (deny wildcards and broad CIDRs)
package terraform.authz

deny["msg"] {
  input.change.resource_type == "aws_iam_role" 
  input.change.after.assume_role_policy ?
  some i
  input.change.after.assume_role_policy contains "*"
  msg = "wildcard principals not allowed"
}

deny["msg"] {
  input.change.resource_type == "aws_security_group_rule" 
  contains(input.change.after.cidr_blocks[], "/0")
  msg = "broad CIDR not allowed"
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test this gating with tfjson diff and CI? 
- How to handle exceptions for legitimate wildcard use (e.g., VPC endpoints) while keeping guardrails?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical knowledge of wiring tags, backends, and CI gates for Snowflake resources in Terraform.

## Key Concepts
- Wrapper modules and tag propagation to child resources
- Provider aliases for multi-environment configurations
- CI gates with fmt/validate/tflint and plan filtering for environment-specific changes

## Code Examples

### 1) Wrapper Module
```terraform
# wrapper/main.tf
variable "environment" { type = string }
variable "cost_center" { type = string }
variable "additional_tags" { type = map(string) default = {} }

module "snowflake" {
  source = "./modules/snowflake"
  tags = merge(
    var.additional_tags,
    { Environment = var.environment, CostCenter = var.cost_center }
  )
}
```

### 2) Backend & Provider Alias
```terraform
# backend.tf
terraform {
  backend "remote" {
    hostname     = "app.terraform.io"
    organization = "your-org"
    workspaces {
      name = "snowflake-dev"
    }
  }
}

# providers.tf
provider "snowflake" {
  alias  = "dev"
  region = "us-east-1"
}
```

### 3) GitHub Actions Workflow
```yaml
# .github/workflows/terraform.yml
name: Terraform
on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - '**.tf'
      - '.github/workflows/**'

jobs:
  terraform:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
      - run: terraform fmt -check
      - run: terraform validate
      - run: tflint
      - run: terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
      - name: Check for prod changes
        run: |-
          if grep -q "prod" <<< "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"; then
            echo "Cannot modify prod in dev workflow"
            exit 1
          fi
```

## Variable Management
- Define input variables in variables.tf with appropriate type constraints and descriptions
- Create dedicated .tfvars files for each environment (dev.tfvars, staging.tfvars, prod.tfvars)
- Execute deployments with terraform apply -var-file=environment.tfvars

## Workspace Strategy
- Utilize terraform workspace new dev/staging/prod for environment isolation
- Each workspace maintains its own state file automatically
- Prevents accidental cross-environment resource modifications

## DRY Implementation
- Employ locals.tf for computed and derived values
- Reference variables consistently across all resource blocks
- Restrict environment-specific values exclusively to .tfvars files
- Maintain shared configuration logic in the main .tf files

```hcl
module "wrapper" {
  source = "./modules/wrapper"
  environment = var.environment
  
  modules = {
    network = module.network
    app     = module.app
    data    = module.data
  }
}
```

## CI Gating Strategy
```bash
# CI script to validate plan components
terraform plan -out=tfplan -json

cat tfplan | jq -r '.planned_values.root_module.resources[] | .address' | \
  grep -v "^module\.\(network\|app\|data\)" && exit 1
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Key Concepts
- Terraform plan JSON parsing
- Secret-detection in tfvars
- CI gate integration per environment

## Code Example
```python
import sys, json, re, glob
pattern = re.compile(r'(?i)(password|secret|token|aws_secret_access_key|db_password)')
for path in glob.glob('environments/**/*.tfvars', recursive=True):
  with open(path) as f:
    for line in f:
      if pattern.search(line) and '=' in line:
        print(f'Secret detected in {path}: {line.strip()}')
        sys.exit(1)
```
